long_biography.plain_text:
When Primo Smallgoods launched in Western Sydney in 1985, Paul Lederer was among its first employees, working in the food-manufacturing business founded by his uncle Andrew. He developed his career inside the company rather than founding it himself. After Andrew's death, Lederer inherited the family stake and led the enterprise through further production growth, acquisitions and national distribution.

Affinity Equity Partners later bought a majority interest, while the Lederer family retained a minority holding. JBS acquired the group in 2015 in a transaction valued at A$1.45 billion, completing the exit from the business that created Lederer's fortune. He subsequently built a diversified family office spanning property, investments and food manufacturing. He now controls Consolidated Real Foods Group, is a founding partner and chairman of 3 Capital, and serves as chairman and co-owner of Western Sydney Wanderers. The football role is a separate ownership and governance position, not the source of the operating assets or wealth attributed to his food and investment businesses.
